output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, Celsius Holdings—the energy-drink company—faces the Nielsen and Valente proposed consumer class actions, filed October 26 and 28, alleging misleading product-label claims about metabolism and fat burning. A separate September 4 securities class action alleges misleading disclosures about Alani Nu’s health risks, marketing and compliance practices. Other unresolved matters disclosed in its November 5 filing include Pepsi-distribution-related securities litigation, related shareholder derivative actions that are stayed, a consumer lawsuit concerning social-media promoters’ financial relationships, and an Eniva trademark dispute. Celsius settled the Flo Rida/Strong Arm endorsement-and-licensing litigation on September 4 for $85 million, without admitting wrongdoing or liability. It also has indemnification exposure in the Larissa Rodriguez wrongful-death lawsuit against Alani Nu distributors Glazer’s, but Celsius itself was not a named defendant in that case.
caveats: This answer concerns Celsius Holdings and its energy-drink business, not the separate cryptocurrency company Celsius Network.
The pending complaints contain allegations, not findings of liability; Celsius disputes the claims. Case statuses reflect the November 5, 2026 company filing and may have changed afterward.

key_facts.fact: Valente v. Celsius Holdings was filed in the Northern District of Illinois, alleging misleading or inadequately substantiated product-label statements.
Nielsen v. Celsius Holdings was filed against Celsius Holdings and Celsius, Inc. in the Western District of Washington; the consumer claims concern metabolism and fat-burning representations.
A marketing-practices securities class action was filed in the Southern District of Florida over alleged misleading disclosures concerning Alani Nu health risks, marketing and compliance.
The company disclosed continuing Pepsi-distribution-related securities litigation; after dismissal with leave to replead, an amended complaint and another dismissal motion had been filed.
Related shareholder derivative actions were stayed pending specified developments in the securities litigation.
A California consumer class action concerning alleged financial relationships with social-media promoters remained in litigation following amendment and a renewed dismissal motion.
Celsius and Eniva remained in litigation over VIBE-formative trademarks, including Eniva's infringement counterclaims.
Celsius agreed to an $85 million settlement resolving the Flo Rida/Strong Arm endorsement-and-licensing litigation without admitting wrongdoing or liability, as disclosed in its November 5 filing.
In the Larissa Rodriguez wrongful-death action against Glazer's distributors, Celsius disclosed an indemnification obligation but said it was not a named defendant.

citations.title: Celsius Holdings, Inc. 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026
excerpts: _Nielsen and Valente Class Actions_ On October 26, 2026, a putative consumer class action, Nielsen v. Celsius Holdings, Inc., was filed against the Company and Celsius, Inc. in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington.
On October 28, 2026, a nearly identical putative class action, Valente v. Celsius Holdings, Inc., was filed against the Company in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois.

The complaint alleges that the defendants made materially false or misleading statements and failed to disclose material information concerning the health risks associated with Alani Nu energy drinks, the marketing of Alani Nu products, and the Company’s compliance practices.

_California Consumer Class Action_ On January 22, 2025, the Company and certain individuals were named as defendants in a putative class action filed in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California. The complaint alleges, on behalf of a putative nationwide class of all purchasers of Celsius products, that plaintiff and other class members were misled regarding the alleged financial relationship between Celsius and the individual defendants, who allegedly promoted the Company’s products on social media.

_Eniva Trademark Litigation Concerning Vibe-Formative Marks_ On March 20, 2025, the Company filed a declaratory judgment action against Eniva after Eniva alleged before the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board that the Company’s VIBE-formative marks were likely to cause confusion with Eniva’s registered VIBE mark used in connection with liquid dietary supplements. The declaratory judgment action was filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota, seeking a declaration that the Company’s use and registration of its marks do not infringe Eniva’s trademark rights. On April 10, 2025, Eniva filed its answer and counterclaims, asserting, among other things, that the Company's use of the VIBE-formative marks constitutes trademark infringement under federal and state law, false designation of origin and unfair competition. Eniva further seeks an order declaring that the Company is not entitled to register its marks.

The Company is not currently named as a defendant, but the matter relates to Alani Nu products and the Company has an obligation to indemnify the named defendants for a loss arising out of any actual or alleged injury or damages suffered in connection with the consumption or purchase of Alani Nu.

excerpts: The Company and individual executives were named as defendants in two putative securities class actions, both filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida and concerning, among other things, allegedly false and misleading statements or omissions concerning the Company’s distribution agreement with Pepsi and the Company’s growth. The first putative securities class action was filed on November 22, 2024. The complaint asserted claims for violations of Section 10(b) of the Exchange Act, Rule 10b-5 promulgated thereunder and Section 20(a) of the Exchange Act. The second putative securities class action was filed on January 14, 2025. The complaint also asserted claims for violations of Section 10(b) of the Exchange Act, Rule 10b-5 promulgated thereunder and Section 20(a) of the Exchange Act. On March 3, 2025, the Court consolidated the two actions (the “ Securities Class Action ” ) and appointed lead plaintiff and lead counsel. The lead plaintiff filed an amended complaint on April 25, 2025, naming the Company, its CEO, CFO and Chief of Staff as defendants. The amended complaint asserts claims for violations of Section 10(b) of the Exchange Act, Rule 10b-5 promulgated thereunder and Section 20(a) of the Exchange Act. The amended complaint was filed on behalf of stockholders who purchased or otherwise acquired shares of the Company’s stock between May 9, 2023 and November 5, 2024.

All of the derivative actions have been stayed unless and until: (i) the Securities Class Action is dismissed with prejudice, and all appeals related thereto have been exhausted; or (ii) the pending motion to dismiss in the Securities Class Action is denied in full or in part.

On September 4, 2026, the Company entered into a settlement agreement with the plaintiffs resolving the lawsuits and all related claims between the parties. Under the settlement agreement, without admitting any wrongdoing or liability, the Company agreed to pay the plaintiffs an aggregate amount of $ 85\.0 million, consisting of $ 60\.0 million paid on September 15, 2026 and $ 25\.0 million payable on January 5, 2027. The settlement amount equals the amount the Company previously reported and accrued as of prior quarter end in connection with these matters. As of September 30, 2026, the remaining unpaid balance of $ 25\.0 million was recorded in other current liabilities on the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets.
